house.description: Department of Health required to employ a public health school health services consultant.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Health Finance and Policy

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to health; requiring the Department of Health to employ a public health school health services consultant; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 144.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[144.063] PUBLIC HEALTH SCHOOL HEALTH SERVICES CONSULTANT. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Employment of public health school health services consultant.+]

[+The Department of Health must employ a public health school health services consultant to improve health and educational outcomes among children and adolescents in educational settings. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Requirements for position.+]

[+The public health school health services consultant employed by the department under subdivision 1 must be a registered nurse who: +]

[+(1) is registered as a public health nurse in Minnesota; +]

[+(2) is licensed as a school nurse in Minnesota; +]

[+(3) has a minimum of three years of experience as a licensed school nurse serving schools; +]

[+(4) has demonstrated expertise in public health nursing as it relates to school health for children and adolescents in educational settings; and +]

[+(5) possesses comprehensive knowledge of population-based school health issues, access to health services in schools, public health principles, health education, school-based health services, and the relationship between health and educational outcomes. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Duties.+]

[+The public health school health services consultant employed by the department under subdivision 1 must: +]

[+(1) develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain state and local policies and programs that address the health needs of children and adolescents in educational settings; +]

[+(2) support educational institutions in sustaining and advancing professional skills in school health leadership, health communication, and health promotion; +]

[+(3) provide technical assistance, guidance, training, and consultation on school health best practices that enhance the health and well-being of children and adolescents in educational settings; +]

[+(4) identify, develop, and distribute resources on school health best practices to enhance the capacity and readiness of school nurses and other school health professionals to effectively and safely meet the health needs of children and adolescents in educational settings; +]

[+(5) develop and disseminate guidance for school nurses and other school health professionals on the effective implementation of health promotion activities; +]

[+(6) expand access to online and asynchronous continuing education and professional development programs for school nurses and other school health professionals, with a focus on best practices that support the health and well-being of children and adolescents in educational settings; +]

[+(7) collect school health workforce data to evaluate the effectiveness of health services provided in educational settings; +]

[+(8) collaborate with the Department of Education; school-based health centers as defined in section 145.903, subdivision 1; and other state agencies to coordinate health-related services for children and adolescents in educational settings; and +]

[+(9) provide the services and supports described in clauses (1) to (8) to public health departments, schools, and national agencies, as necessary, to address the health-related needs of children and adolescents in educational settings. +]
additions: [144.063] PUBLIC HEALTH SCHOOL HEALTH SERVICES CONSULTANT.
Subdivision 1.
Employment of public health school health services consultant.
The Department of Health must employ a public health school health services consultant to improve health and educational outcomes among children and adolescents in educational settings.
Subd. 2.
Requirements for position.
The public health school health services consultant employed by the department under subdivision 1 must be a registered nurse who:
(1) is registered as a public health nurse in Minnesota;
(2) is licensed as a school nurse in Minnesota;
(3) has a minimum of three years of experience as a licensed school nurse serving schools;
(4) has demonstrated expertise in public health nursing as it relates to school health for children and adolescents in educational settings; and

(5) possesses comprehensive knowledge of population-based school health issues, access to health services in schools, public health principles, health education, school-based health services, and the relationship between health and educational outcomes.
Subd. 3.
Duties.
The public health school health services consultant employed by the department under subdivision 1 must:
(1) develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain state and local policies and programs that address the health needs of children and adolescents in educational settings;
(2) support educational institutions in sustaining and advancing professional skills in school health leadership, health communication, and health promotion;
(3) provide technical assistance, guidance, training, and consultation on school health best practices that enhance the health and well-being of children and adolescents in educational settings;

(4) identify, develop, and distribute resources on school health best practices to enhance the capacity and readiness of school nurses and other school health professionals to effectively and safely meet the health needs of children and adolescents in educational settings;
(5) develop and disseminate guidance for school nurses and other school health professionals on the effective implementation of health promotion activities;

(6) expand access to online and asynchronous continuing education and professional development programs for school nurses and other school health professionals, with a focus on best practices that support the health and well-being of children and adolescents in educational settings;
(7) collect school health workforce data to evaluate the effectiveness of health services provided in educational settings;

(8) collaborate with the Department of Education; school-based health centers as defined in section 145.903, subdivision 1; and other state agencies to coordinate health-related services for children and adolescents in educational settings; and

(9) provide the services and supports described in clauses (1) to (8) to public health departments, schools, and national agencies, as necessary, to address the health-related needs of children and adolescents in educational settings.
